chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated that Ibn Muni’a said: Mus’ab narrated to me that Malik said: I was narrated from Aba Abdul Rahman, from Hafs ibn Asem, from Abi Sa’id al-Khidry, or from Abi Hurayrah.

He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Seven people will be shaded by God, the Mighty and Exalted, in His shade on the day when there is no shade except His shade: a just Imam, a youth who grew up in the worship of God, the Mighty and Exalted, a man whose heart is attached to the mosque when he leaves it until he returns to it, two men who were in obedience to God, the Mighty and Exalted, so they gathered upon that and then separated, a man who remembered God, the Mighty and Exalted, in solitude and his eyes flowed with tears from the fear of God, the Mighty and Exalted, a man whom a woman of good lineage and beauty invited and he said: Indeed I fear God, the Mighty and Exalted, and a man who gave charity and concealed it so that his left hand did not know what his right hand gave in charity.'

key_terms.شَابٌّ نَشَأَ فِي عِبَادَةِ اللَّهِ: Youth who grew up in worship of God
key_terms.صَدَقَةٌ بِضَمَارِهَا: Charity given in secrecy (implied by left hand not knowing what right hand gave)
key_terms.يَوْمَ لَا ظِلَّ إِلَّا ظِلُّهُ: The day when there is no shade except His

ai.seo_question: Who are the seven people who will be shaded by God on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a comprehensive guide to spiritual excellence, emphasizing that divine protection on the Day of Resurrection is granted not merely through ritual, but through consistent moral character and sincerity. The inclusion of 'an Imam who is just' highlights the Shia emphasis on righteous leadership, while the detailed descriptions of secret charity and solitary weeping underscore the importance of khulus (purity of intention) in Shia piety.
